html:
A space probe from the United Arab Emirates, called Hope, launched from Japan's Tanegashima Space Center on 20 July 2020. It went into orbit around Mars on 9 February 2021, the first Arab mission to reach another planet.

Hope studies the Martian atmosphere and weather. Its wide orbit lets it watch the whole planet at all times of day and through the seasons, to learn how dust storms form and how Mars is losing its air to space.

Emirati engineers built it with help from American universities, above all the University of Colorado. The team of some 200 Emiratis was young, and many were women. The aim was as much to build skills and a science economy at home, looking past oil, as to study Mars. The project was led by Omran Sharaf; its science lead, Sarah Al Amiri, was also a government minister. Arriving in the year of the country's fiftieth anniversary was part of the plan.

India had reached Mars orbit with its Mars Orbiter Mission in 2014, the first Asian nation to do so.
